scenarios.description: Controlled single rejection followed by recovery; documentation-based error envelope, not measured live outage parity.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='recovery_rate_limited' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: Controlled single rejection followed by recovery; documentation-based error envelope, not measured live outage parity.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='recovery_server_error' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: Hold one controlled error response for 15 seconds. This exceeds the 12-second provider-request deadline observed in the Replit receipt test and remains inside FetchSandbox's 20-second outer webhook deadline. Score recovery only when the app webhook fails and redelivery starts before the twin releases the response; a later 503 alone is not timeout proof. Apps with longer provider-request deadlines need a longer fault hold.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='recovery_timeout' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: Accept the email, then withhold its HTTP response for 15 seconds. Observe whether a Replit-style 12-second provider request timeout causes the app to retry safely.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='accepted_response_loss' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: The address hard-bounces. Resend accepts the send, then reports it was never delivered — your handler must suppress the address, not just log a 200.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='email_bounced' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: The recipient marks the email as spam. Keep sending to them and your domain reputation suffers.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='recipient_complained' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: Your sending domain has not finished DNS verification, so Resend refuses the send. This is a sender problem, not a bad recipient.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='domain_unverified' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: The API key is rejected. A permanent failure — retrying will never succeed and only burns quota.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='auth_failure' to quickrun or run_workflow

scenarios.description: Resend delivers the same webhook more than once. Every event arrives 3 times with the same svix-id — if your handler suppresses or records on each delivery instead of de-duplicating, you do the work three times.
scenarios.how_to_run: pass scenario='webhook_duplicate_delivery' to quickrun or run_workflow
